# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

=====
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in

   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;

3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames

4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no

5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38377942056) · started 09:41 · done 11:16 ✅

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
=====
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38377942056) · started 09:41 · done 11:16 ✅

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
=====
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on OR…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
=====
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on OR…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
=====
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in

3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1587
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1587
- **Title**: gh-1572 [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1572` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +444
- **Deletions**: -82
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T11:16:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T16:38:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1572
### Root Cause

Starting `fa` rewrote `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` on every boot: the boot's `persistConfig` (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) constructed a **new** `CliConfig(...)` passing only some fields, so every parsed section it did not mention (`spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, `power.hold`, `auto_update`) reset to defaults in the object being saved. Two cooperating leaks: `CliConfig.withCustomProviders` — the copy helper inside `saveCliConfig`'s merge-before-write — had drifted the same way (also dropping `spills`/`subagents`/`waiting`/`jobs`/`agentMode`/`misuseBreaker`/`streamThinking`), and the `_diskPreservedSections` disk backstop did not list the dropped keys, so nothing re-attached them from disk.

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`:
  - complete `copyWith` (every parsed field, null = keep); `withCustomProviders` is now a `copyWith` delegation so the copy list can never drift again;
  - `toYaml()` renders `spills:` (new `SpillsConfig.toYaml()`, non-defaults only) and `agent.misuseBreaker: false`;
  - `_diskPreservedSections` extended to every known top-level key (`spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `power`, `auto_update`);
  - `saveCliConfig` skips the temp-file+rename when the merged output is byte-identical to the on-disk text — no write at boot when nothing changed.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: `persistConfig` builds `saved.copyWith(<live session overlays only>)` — every section rides along from the loaded config by construction; the provider/model triple keeps the loaded seed (explicit `--provider/--base-url/--model` still never change saved defaults). `compaction:` rides along as the loaded global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds.

### Test Coverage

- `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` (new, 6 tests): the ticket's config round-trips `loadCliConfig` → persist-shaped save → `saveCliConfig` with every section intact; the boot-shaped overlay save keeps the provider triple and every section; `toYaml` renders (and omits-at-defaults) `spills:`; the disk backstop re-attaches every omitted block; an unchanged save does not rewrite the file (mtime pinned). All 6 failed before the fix, pass after.
- End-to-end (isolated `HOME`, the ticket's exact command): boot keeps every user section and renders `spills:`; a second boot performs no write (unchanged mtime).
- Full suite: ~4000 test groups green. The 19 failures in the local full run are all pre-existing environmental noise, each proven: 14 spawn-fa integration tests are hijacked by the runner's own `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env (children reach a real provider instead of the mock) — they pass with the vars unset and fail identically on the base commit; the 5 `browser_ext` tests hit Chrome service-worker/D-Bus infra on this runner — the base commit fails the identical 5. No product-code regressions.

### Notes

- The first boot after this fix may canonicalize section order/formatting once (typed render of carried sections); content-equivalent, and subsequent boots with no change perform no write at all.
- `waiting:` still has no typed renderer — its raw on-disk block is the only faithful form and now survives saves via the backstop (same mechanism as `memory:`/`a2a:`).
- `compaction:` rides along from the LOADED global value only (never the settings-hub live override or a project pick), so the documented no-leak guarantee is unchanged.

# gh-1572: [BUG] fa boot rewrites ~/.fah/config.yaml and drops sections (spills, subagents, jobs, headless, agent, quota, tui, trajectory)

## Description

## Summary
Starting `fa` (verified on 1.0.565 and origin/main d5fd213d; first reported on 1.0.547) rewrites the global `~/.fah/config.yaml` from a freshly built `CliConfig` and silently loses user sections.

## Reproduction (isolated HOME)
```
mkdir -p /tmp/h/.fah
# config.yaml with: provider/model/baseUrl + spills, subagents, jobs, headless,
# agent (mode: pi), quota (badge: true), tui (theme: ohmypi-dark), trajectory (wireDump: true)
HOME=/tmp/h OPENAI_API_KEY=x fa --provider openai-completions --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1/v1 --model zzz -p x
```
Result: `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory` are gone; `mode: code`, `approvalMode: yolo`, `allowedTools: []` are added.

Note: in my run a plain `fa -p x` (no flags) and `fa --model zzz -p x` did the same, so the flags are not the only trigger. Any boot whose canonical rendering differs from the file rewrites it.

## Root cause (from code)
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (~1553-1625): `persistConfig` builds a NEW `CliConfig(...)` carrying only some fields (provider/model/baseUrl, mode, approval, roles, ttsr, customProviders, models, mcp, skills, cube, tools, memory, redact, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, power). It does NOT pass `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent` (`contextWindowCap`/`agentLoadMode`/`stuckTool`), `quota`, `tuiTheme`/`statusLine`, `wireDump`, `waiting`.
- `CliConfig.toYaml()` (`lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` ~944-1040) never renders `spills:`.
- The backstop `_diskPreservedSections` (~1664) does not list `spills`, `subagents`, `jobs`, `headless`, `agent`, `quota`, `tui`, `trajectory`, `waiting`, so they are not re-attached from disk.
- `persistConfig()` is also called unconditionally once at boot (~1627), so merely launching fa triggers the rewrite.

## Expected
- Saving never drops a known section: carry every parsed field through `persistConfig` (use `saved` as the base, e.g. a `copyWith`), render `spills:` in `toYaml`, and extend the disk-preservation backstop to all known top-level keys the caller did not render.
- Explicit per-launch flags (`--provider/--base-url/--model`) must not change the saved defaults (add a test to pin this).
- No write at boot when nothing changed.

## Regression tests
1. `saveCliConfig` round trip: a config.yaml with every known section survives `loadCliConfig` -> persistConfig-shaped `CliConfig` -> `saveCliConfig`.
2. `toYaml` renders `spills:` when set.
3. Boot with `--provider/--base-url/--model` leaves provider/model/baseUrl and all sections unchanged.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38377942056) · started 09:41 · done 11:16 ✅
