1. `_clearContextCap` (settings → clear context cap, drops `agent:` block from file) → any later `persistConfig()` in the same session (mode switch, approval change, skills toggle…) re-renders `agent: contextWindowCap: 256000` from the stale boot snapshot — the user's removal is silently reverted.
2. `_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings → auto update cycle off→notify, drops `auto_update:` from file) → later persist re-adds `auto_update: false`.

Before this PR these removals stuck (the fresh-CliConfig emitter rendered neither key and the old backstop didn't re-attach them). So the PR trades "boot drops sections" for "same-session removals resurrect". The removal flows' contract ("contextWindowCap removed → file", "auto_update removed → notify is the default") is broken by the next save.

Severity: this is a correctness bug introduced by the diff — the settings flows' documented behavior ("removed → …", "everything else survives byte-for-byte") is broken. Per the verdict rules this is 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug). It's the same class of bug as the ticket itself (config file not honoring user intent). It affects two settings-hub flows.

Wait — one consideration: were these removal flows EVER safe before gh-1572? Let me re-verify the pre-PR behavior with a quick check on the base commit. Actually I reasoned through the code: pre-PR persistConfig fresh CliConfig without contextWindowCap/autoUpdate → emitter omits both → old backstop (memory, cube, roles, ttsr, prompts, redact, compaction, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, mcp, links, output) doesn't include agent/auto_update → removals stuck. I could verify by `git stash`-free worktree... Actually I can verify by checking out base cli_config.dart + fah_runapp.dart into a temp dir? Simpler: `git worktree`? AGENTS.md says avoid. I can simulate the old persist shape in my scratch test: `saveCliConfig(tmp, CliConfig(mode:'code', approvalMode:'yolo', allowedTools:[]))` after the drop — with the NEW code the backstop includes agent/auto_update but the emitter (fresh CliConfig) doesn't render them → re-attached → also resurrects! Wait — that's the "disk backstop" test behavior — deliberate. Hmm! So even the OLD persist shape now resurrects (because the backstop now includes agent/auto_update).

Hold on, that's an important nuance: the disk backstop's added keys (`agent`, `auto_update`, etc.) mean ANY save from a config that doesn't carry them resurrects on-disk values. That's the PR's explicit intent ("a save can never silently delete one") — resurrection-by-design forgetful callers. The removal flows are exactly "a caller that wants to delete a section" — and they DON'T go through saveCliConfig at all; they edit the file directly. The problem is the NEXT save (from the stale snapshot) clobbers their file edit. The backstop makes it worse in the fresh-CliConfig shape; the saved.copyWith base makes it happen in the boot shape. Either way: post-PR, in-session removals are undone by the next save. Pre-PR, both the emitter and backstop left agent/auto_update alone, so removals stuck.

Let me quickly double-check pre-PR behavior by running the scratch repro against the base commit to be rigorous. I can do this without touching the user's tree: create a detached worktree? AGENTS.md wants me to ask the user first... but this is a CI job checkout, and the harness explicitly blesses `git diff`/`git show` for review. A worktree for a 2-minute verification is borderline; AGENTS.md says ask first by default. Alternative: `git show origin/main:lib/src/cli_config.dart` — I already read the diff; the old `_diskPreservedSections` lacked agent/auto_update (confirmed in the diff), and the old persistConfig didn't carry contextWindowCap/autoUpdate (confirmed in diff). The old emitter's `_agentSectionYaml` from a fresh CliConfig: contextWindowCap null, agentLoadMode null, stuckYaml '' , misuseBreaker true → returns ''. autoUpdate default notify → renders nothing. So the removals stuck pre-PR. Solid — no need for a worktree run.

Actually wait, one more wrinkle for the pre-PR auto_update case: pre-PR the persist save rewrote the file from a fresh CliConfig — and for the cap-clear case, pre-PR the save would ALSO rewrite the whole file lossy-style (dropping e.g. spills etc. — the ticket bug!) but NOT the agent/auto_update keys. So pre-PR: removals stick, other sections drop. Post-PR: sections preserved, removals undone. Both broken, differently. The PR fixes the headline bug but breaks the two removal flows.

Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? Machine protocol: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior". This is broken behavior of shipped settings flows introduced by the diff. I'll mark BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. A reasonable fix: overlay the live AgentCliConfig values that the settings flows mutate (`autoUpdate`, `contextWindowCap`) in persistConfig — e.g. `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate`, `contextWindowCap: cli.config.contextWindowCap` (need to check AgentCliConfig exposes them — `config.autoUpdate = next` exists in settings_flow_auto_update.dart, so yes; `config.contextWindowCap` is read in _clearContextCap). OR: the settings flows should update the in-memory `saved`… but `saved` is local to _runApp; persistConfig closure could read from `cli.config`. Cleanest: pass those two live fields in the copyWith like mode/approvalMode.

Wait, does AgentCliConfig have `contextWindowCap`? _clearContextCap checks `config.contextWindowCap == null` — yes. And `config.autoUpdate` — yes.

Now let me also check: are there other flows that mutate file-level state that `saved` overlays would clobber? `skillsAccess` — persistConfig overlays from live. `skillToggles` — live. `cube` — live (cli.config.cubeSettings). `models`, `mcp`, `tools`, `modelRoles`, `customProviders` — live. `mode`/`approvalMode`/`allowedTools` — live. What about `ttsr`? persistConfig no longer passes ttsr — `saved.ttsr` rides along. Is there a live flow mutating ttsr? Let me check: "TTSR rules are static per session" comment (removed in the diff). ttsr static per session — fine.

`promptOverrides`: static per session — fine.
`memory`, `redact`, `a2a`, `providerTimeouts`, `images`, `fabric`, `power*`, `quota`, `tui*`, `links`, `streamThinking`, `wireDump`, `spills`, `subagents`, `waiting`, `jobs`, `headless` — all ride from saved. Any live mutators? Let me grep for flows that write these to the file mid-session: quota badge? Let me search for `quota` upserts, `tui` upserts, `power` upserts, `redact` flows.

- settings_flow.dart has Compaction flows (write via upsert) — compaction rides from saved. The PR comment says compaction global/project flows write via targeted upsert themselves; the live override is never persisted. But the same resurrection question: user picks global compaction engine in settings (writes `compaction:` to file via upsert), `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value → next persist re-renders `compaction:` from saved → REVERT of the user's global pick! Wait — pre-PR: persistConfig deliberately did NOT carry compaction and the backstop INCLUDED 'compaction' → the on-disk block (written by the upsert) survived. Post-PR: emitter renders `compaction:` from saved.compactionEngine (boot value) → "caller wins wherever it rendered" → the upsert-written block is replaced by the boot-stale value. Let me verify the compaction render: `_compactionYaml()` renders engine/judgeBudgetSeconds when non-default presumably. If user's boot value was default (nothing on disk), settings writes `compaction:\n  engine: classic\n` to the file; next persist: saved.compactionEngine == default (structured?) → renders '' → backstop sees compaction rendered? No — emitter omitted → backstop re-attaches the on-disk `compaction:` block → SURVIVES. But if the boot file HAD `compaction: engine: classic` and the user switches to structured via settings: settings upsert removes/rewrites `compaction:` (engine: structured — is structured renderable? default). Let me check the compaction flow: does dropping to default remove the block? If boot had classic (non-default), saved.compactionEngine == classic; user switches t…
Both regressions **confirmed**. Let me also check the compaction settings flow — the PR now carries `compaction:` from the stale boot snapshot where the old code deliberately left it to the backstop.

This is important. The auto_update settings flow (`_dropAutoUpdateKey`) uses `_dropTopLevelBlock` to remove the `auto_update:` key from the file directly — a surgical edit. This does NOT go through `saveCliConfig`, so the backstop doesn't fight it... UNLESS a subsequent `persistConfig()` (triggered by another settings change, `/mode` switch, etc.) happens afterward with the in-memory `saved.autoUpdate` still holding the OLD value. Wait — let me trace: `_dropAutoUpdateKey` edits the FILE. Then `config.autoUpdate = next` updates the live AgentCliConfig. But `persistConfig` uses `saved` — the CliConfig loaded at boot — as the base! `saved.autoUpdate` is still whatever was loaded at boot (e.g. `off`), NOT the live `config.autoUpdate`.

So: boot with `auto_update: off` in the file → user cycles the settings-hub Auto update flow to `notify` → the file gets the key dropped. Then ANY subsequent persistConfig trigger (e.g. `/mode` switch, skills toggle, models change) writes `saved.copyWith(...)` — `saved.autoUpdate` is still `AutoUpdateMode.off` (loaded at boot) → emitter renders `auto_update: false` → the dropped key is RE-ADDED to the file!

Wait, actually is this a pre-existing issue or introduced by this PR? Before this PR, `persistConfig` built a fresh `CliConfig(...)` and did NOT pass `autoUpdate` → defaulted to `AutoUpdateMode.notify` → emitter rendered nothing → the old backstop (which did NOT include `auto_update`) didn't re-attach → the file lost the `auto_update:` line. Hmm, so before the PR, the settings flow's file edit would ALSO be lost (the key would be dropped from the file by the next persistConfig save — actually before the fix the whole file was being rewritten lossy anyway).

Hold on — actually before this PR, the next `persistConfig` rewrote the file from the fresh CliConfig — `auto_update` default `notify` renders nothing → and `auto_update` was NOT in `_diskPreservedSections` → the line vanished. So the settings flow's `off` choice was ALSO reverted (dropped) by the next save before this PR. Both before and after, there's an incoherence: `persistConfig` doesn't overlay the LIVE `config.autoUpdate`.

After this PR: the file keeps whatever was loaded at boot (`saved.autoUpdate`) — the settings-hub change to the file gets reverted to the boot-loaded value (if different). So if user cycles `off → notify` (drop key), then any later persistConfig re-adds `auto_update: false` from the stale `saved`. The user's drop is undone. That's a regression vs. the intent of `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, though arguably consistent with "rides along from the LOADED global value". But the PR description says the guarantee is about sections not being dropped; here a user change made mid-session via the settings hub is silently reverted by the next save. Before the PR, the same flow: user cycles `notify → on` → file gets `auto_update: true` via upsert → next persistConfig save: fresh CliConfig without autoUpdate → renders nothing → old backstop doesn't have auto_update → the key is DROPPED. So before the PR the setting was lost too (even worse). After the PR, cycling notify→on then a later save: `saved.autoUpdate` = notify (loaded at boot) → renders nothing → the `auto_update: true` line the settings flow wrote is dropped... wait no — `auto_update` IS now in `_diskPreservedSections`, so the emitter-omitted on-disk block is RE-ATTACHED. So cycling notify→on → file has `auto_update: true` → next persistConfig: `saved.autoUpdate`=notify renders nothing → backstop re-attaches `auto_update: true` from disk.

So the case that regresses: user cycles OFF→NOTIFY within a session (drops the key from file), then a later persistConfig in the same session re-renders `auto_update: false` from the stale booted `saved.autoUpdate == off`. The in-memory `saved` was never updated. The file flip-flops back to `off`. This is a genuine (if narrow) correctness gap: `persistConfig` should overlay the live `config.autoUpdate` (like it does for mode/approvalMode etc.), or the settings flow should update `saved`'s copy. Actually wait — does the settings flow update `saved`? `config.autoUpdate = next` — `config` here is the AgentCliConfig (live), not `saved` (the CliConfig captured in the closure). So yes, `saved` stays stale.

Hmm, but is this within scope of this PR? The PR claims: "compaction: rides along from the LOADED global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds". For compaction that's INTENTIONAL (session scope promises no file change). For auto_update, the settings flow EXPLICITLY writes the global file — it's a global-scope pick — so carrying the boot-loaded value and NOT the live value means the next save reverts the user's file-level change. Before this PR: same revert happened (key dropped entirely, both `on` and `off` choices lost). So this PR doesn't make that specific case worse — for `off→notify` it actually makes it WORSE in a subtle way: before, the key vanished (matching the user's intent — notify is default), after, the key comes back as `auto_update: false` (contradicting the user's intent). Let me double check: user boots with `auto_update: off` in file. `saved.autoUpdate == off`. User cycles: notify→... wait the flow cycles based on `config.autoUpdate` which at boot == off (loaded). Cycle: off → notify → `_dropAutoUpdateKey()` removes the line from the file. `config.autoUpdate = notify`. blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Same for `agent:` block with hand comments: post-PR emitter renders typed subset → comments lost once. Documented. OK — SUGGESTION-level at most, arguably by design.

Now `waiting:` — no renderer, backstop only. Boot save: saved.waiting parsed but never rendered → omitted → backstop re-attaches raw block. Fine.

What about sections in `_diskPreservedSections` that are rendered only conditionally — `subagents` renders when heartbeat/stall non-default; if user's on-disk subagents block has NON-default values, saved carries them → rendered → fine.

`quota`: `QuotaSection` default; test uses `badge: true, ttl_minutes: 30`. Renderer `_quotaYaml` — presumably renders non-defaults. Fine.

Now let me also check `power:` — `power.hold` has `PowerAssertionHold` with value 'session'. `_powerYaml` renders `hold:`? saw partial: sleepPrevention + presumably hold. Fine.

Next dimension: the `fetchLatestTag` reformat — pure formatter noise, unrelated to the fix. SUG…

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Same for `agent:` block with hand comments: post-PR emitter renders typed subset → comments lost once. Documented. OK — SUGGESTION-level at most, arguably by design.

Now `waiting:` — no renderer, backstop only. Boot save: saved.waiting parsed but never rendered → omitted → backstop re-attaches raw block. Fine.

What about sections in `_diskPreservedSections` that are rendered only conditionally — `subagents` renders when heartbeat/stall non-default; if user's on-disk subagents block has NON-default values, saved carries them → rendered → fine.

`quota`: `QuotaSection` default; test uses `badge: true, ttl_minutes: 30`. Renderer `_quotaYaml` — presumably renders non-defaults. Fine.

Now let me also check `power:` — `power.hold` has `PowerAssertionHold` with value 'session'. `_powerYaml` renders `hold:`? saw partial: sleepPrevention + presumably hold. Fine.

Next dimension: the `fetchLatestTag` reformat — pure formatter noise, unrelated to the fix. SUG…

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... content.thinking:
`AgentCliConfig` has mutable `autoUpdate` (the settings flow sets `config.autoUpdate = next`) and `contextWindowCap` (final). So the fix directions:
- `autoUpdate`: persistConfig could overlay `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` — the live field is maintained by the flow. But careful: is AgentCliConfig.autoUpdate ONLY mutated by the global flow? settings_flow_auto_update cycles the GLOBAL policy (writes global file, no scope pick). Yes — the auto-update flow is global-only. So overlaying `cli.config.autoUpdate` is safe and fixes the auto_update revert.
- `contextWindowCap`: AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap is final, and `_clearContextCap` doesn't update it. Would need the flow to update `saved` or expose a mutable field.
- `compaction`: session-scope live override must not persist; global/project writes go through the file. The cleanest fix is re-syncing `saved` after sanctioned file writes (e.g. a hook the flows call, or making `saved` a mutable var reloaded after `_upsertConfigYaml` global writes / `_drop*` writes).

I'll present the root cause + fix directions in the comment; the author picks.

Now the remaining review dimensions. Let me look at the full new `copyWith` doc and check one more edge in `saveCliConfig`: `_configTmpCounter` incremented even when skipping — no wait, short-circuit returns BEFORE constructing tmp — good.

Another check — `saveCliConfig` skip means the `.fah` dir may be created but file never created when diskText '' and finalText ''? If config doesn't exist and the config to save renders non-empty (typical), file is created. If it renders EMPTY (all-default CliConfig)... can't happen — toYaml always renders provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode. Fine.

Now, the unchanged-save skip: is `finalText == diskText` the right notion of "unchanged"? finalText is derived as `_preserveDiskSections(diskText, merged.toYaml())`. If disk has sections in a different ORDER than the emitter would render but identical content — the emitted text is compared against the FULL disk text, so any ordering difference → rewrite (canonicalization) once, then stable. Matches the PR note. OK.

What about file permissions? rename replaces the file — pre-existing behavior.

Windows: rename-over failed → delete+rename — unchanged.

Now the `test` dimension: 6 new tests, meaningful assertions, all failed pre-fix per the PR description. The unchanged-save test uses mtime — with 50ms delay; reasonable on CI? mtime granularity on some filesystems is 1s — a rewrite within the same second would NOT bump mtime → false pass? No wait — the test expects mtime UNCHANGED. If a rewrite happened but fs mtime granularity is coarse (1s), lastModifiedSync might return the same value → the assertion would PASS even though the file was rewritten — but they also assert text equality which would still pass (content identical). The mtime pin could be a vacuous pass on coarse-mtime filesystems. They added a 50ms delay to "give the filesystem clock room" — on ext4 with ns timestamps fine; on HFS+/coarse fs the test could vacuously pass. Minor test-robustness nit — SUGGESTION. Actually a stronger signal: `File.stat` `size`/inode change or checking `.tmp` files absence. Eh — the content-compare wouldn't catch a no-op rewrite either (identical content). Could assert no tmp file residue — weak. It's acceptable; keep as SUGGESTION.

The `_dropTopLevelBlock` in settings_flow doesn't continue blocks over comment lines while `_topLevelYamlBlockOf` does — pre-existing, out of diff. Not reportable inline; could be general.

Now, PR description claims end-to-end verification and full suite green (19 pre-existing env failures documented). CI: there's no ci_failures.md input — so CI presumably passing/not reported. Fine.

Scope check: ticket asks for (1) carry every parsed field through persistConfig (done), (2) render spills in toYaml (done), (3) extend backstop (done), (4) explicit flags must not change saved defaults + test (done — persist-shaped test), (5) no write at boot when nothing changed (done + test). Ticket ACs satisfied. The compaction claim in the PR: "compaction: rides along from the LOADED global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds" — the no-leak claim holds, but the revert-of-global-pick hazard is unaddressed (my finding).

One more possible issue: `persistConfig` overlays `customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders` — the `.entries` on a map — pre-existing.

Also `allowedTools: cli.approval.alwaysAllowedTools` — if empty list, copyWith passes `const []` — non-null → replaces. Note: `allowedTools ?? this.allowedTools` — an EMPTY list is meaningful (explicit no-tools) and since `??` only checks null, empty list passes through correctly. Good — this is why null=keep works here.

BUT: `promptOverrides` etc. — `promptOverrides ?? this.promptOverrides` — same. persistConfig no longer passes promptOverrides — keeps saved's. Good.

One subtle thing in copyWith semantics: `mode: cli.currentMode.name` etc. — always non-null → fine.

What about `skillsAccess: skillsAccess` — the local `skillsAccess` var in _runApp — where defined? Pre-existing (was in old code too). OK.

Now double-check the `_agentSectionYaml` change: previously rendered when cap/loadMode/stuckTool present; now also when `!misuseBreaker`. And renders `misuseBreaker: false`. Parse side: `misuseBreaker: agentSection?.misuseBreaker ?? true` — need to confirm the parser reads `misuseBreaker` key. Let me check quickly.

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

`AgentCliConfig` has mutable `autoUpdate` (the settings flow sets `config.autoUpdate = next`) and `contextWindowCap` (final). So the fix directions:
- `autoUpdate`: persistConfig could overlay `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` — the live field is maintained by the flow. But careful: is AgentCliConfig.autoUpdate ONLY mutated by the global flow? settings_flow_auto_update cycles the GLOBAL policy (writes global file, no scope pick). Yes — the auto-update flow is global-only. So overlaying `cli.config.autoUpdate` is safe and fixes the auto_update revert.
- `contextWindowCap`: AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap is final, and `_clearContextCap` doesn't update it. Would need the flow to update `saved` or expose a mutable field.
- `compaction`: session-scope live override must not persist; global/project writes go through the file. The cleanest fix is re-syncing `saved` after sanctioned file writes (e.g. a hook the flows call, or making `saved` a mutable var reloaded after `_upsertConfigYaml` global writes / `_drop*` writes).

I'll present the root cause + fix directions in the comment; the author picks.

Now the remaining review dimensions. Let me look at the full new `copyWith` doc and check one more edge in `saveCliConfig`: `_configTmpCounter` incremented even when skipping — no wait, short-circuit returns BEFORE constructing tmp — good.

Another check — `saveCliConfig` skip means the `.fah` dir may be created but file never created when diskText '' and finalText ''? If config doesn't exist and the config to save renders non-empty (typical), file is created. If it renders EMPTY (all-default CliConfig)... can't happen — toYaml always renders provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode. Fine.

Now, the unchanged-save skip: is `finalText == diskText` the right notion of "unchanged"? finalText is derived as `_preserveDiskSections(diskText, merged.toYaml())`. If disk has sections in a different ORDER than the emitter would render but identical content — the emitted text is compared against the FULL disk text, so any ordering difference → rewrite (canonicalization) once, then stable. Matches the PR note. OK.

What about file permissions? rename replaces the file — pre-existing behavior.

Windows: rename-over failed → delete+rename — unchanged.

Now the `test` dimension: 6 new tests, meaningful assertions, all failed pre-fix per the PR description. The unchanged-save test uses mtime — with 50ms delay; reasonable on CI? mtime granularity on some filesystems is 1s — a rewrite within the same second would NOT bump mtime → false pass? No wait — the test expects mtime UNCHANGED. If a rewrite happened but fs mtime granularity is coarse (1s), lastModifiedSync might return the same value → the assertion would PASS even though the file was rewritten — but they also assert text equality which would still pass (content identical). The mtime pin could be a vacuous pass on coarse-mtime filesystems. They added a 50ms delay to "give the filesystem clock room" — on ext4 with ns timestamps fine; on HFS+/coarse fs the test could vacuously pass. Minor test-robustness nit — SUGGESTION. Actually a stronger signal: `File.stat` `size`/inode change or checking `.tmp` files absence. Eh — the content-compare wouldn't catch a no-op rewrite either (identical content). Could assert no tmp file residue — weak. It's acceptable; keep as SUGGESTION.

The `_dropTopLevelBlock` in settings_flow doesn't continue blocks over comment lines while `_topLevelYamlBlockOf` does — pre-existing, out of diff. Not reportable inline; could be general.

Now, PR description claims end-to-end verification and full suite green (19 pre-existing env failures documented). CI: there's no ci_failures.md input — so CI presumably passing/not reported. Fine.

The compaction claim in the PR: "compaction: rides along from the LOADED global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds" — the no-leak claim holds, but the revert-of-global-pick hazard is unaddressed (my finding).

Good — this is why null=keep works here.

One subtle thing in copyWith semantics: `mode: cli.currentMode.name` etc. — always non-null → fine.

This is important. The auto_update settings flow (`_dropAutoUpdateKey`) uses `_dropTopLevelBlock` to remove the `auto_update:` key from the file directly — a surgical edit. This does NOT go through `saveCliConfig`, so the backstop doesn't fight it... UNLESS a subsequent `persistConfig()` (triggered by another settings change, `/mode` switch, etc.) happens afterward with the in-memory `saved.autoUpdate` still holding the OLD value. Wait — let me trace: `_dropAutoUpdateKey` edits the FILE. Then `config.autoUpdate = next` updates the live AgentCliConfig. But `persistConfig` uses `saved` — the CliConfig loaded at boot — as the base! `saved.autoUpdate` is still whatever was loaded at boot (e.g. `off`), NOT the live `config.autoUpdate`.

So: boot with `auto_update: off` in the file → user cycles the settings-hub Auto update flow to `notify` → the file gets the key dropped. Then ANY subsequent persistConfig trigger (e.g. `/mode` switch, skills toggle, models change) writes `saved.copyWith(...)` — `saved.autoUpdate` is still `AutoUpdateMode.off` (loaded at boot) → emitter renders `auto_update: false` → the dropped key is RE-ADDED to the file!

Wait, actually is this a pre-existing issue or introduced by this PR? Before this PR, `persistConfig` built a fresh `CliConfig(...)` and did NOT pass `autoUpdate` → defaulted to `AutoUpdateMode.notify` → emitter rendered nothing → the old backstop (which did NOT include `auto_update`) didn't re-attach → the file lost the `auto_update:` line. Hmm, so before the PR, the settings flow's file edit would ALSO be lost (the key would be dropped from the file by the next persistConfig save — actually before the fix the whole file was being rewritten lossy anyway).

Hold on — actually before this PR, the next `persistConfig` rewrote the file from the fresh CliConfig — `auto_update` default `notify` renders nothing → and `auto_update` was NOT in `_diskPreservedSections` → the line vanished. So the settings flow's `off` choice was ALSO reverted (dropped) by the next save before this PR. Both before and after, there's an incoherence: `persistConfig` doesn't overlay the LIVE `config.autoUpdate`.

After this PR: the file keeps whatever was loaded at boot (`saved.autoUpdate`) — the settings-hub change to the file gets reverted to the boot-loaded value (if different). So if user cycles `off → notify` (drop key), then any later persistConfig re-adds `auto_update: false` from the stale `saved`. The user's drop is undone. That's a regression vs. the intent of `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, though arguably consistent with "rides along from the LOADED global value". But the PR description says the guarantee is about sections not being dropped; here a user change made mid-session via the settings hub is silently reverted by the next save. Before the PR, the same flow: user cycles `notify → on` → file gets `auto_update: true` via upsert → next persistConfig save: fresh CliConfig without autoUpdate → renders nothing → old backstop doesn't have auto_update → the key is DROPPED. So before the PR the setting was lost too (even worse). After the PR, cycling notify→on then a later save: `saved.autoUpdate` = notify (loaded at boot) → renders nothing → the `auto_update: true` line the settings flow wrote is dropped... wait no — `auto_update` IS now in `_diskPreservedSections`, so the emitter-omitted on-disk block is RE-ATTACHED. So cycling notify→on → file has `auto_update: true` → next persistConfig: `saved.autoUpdate`=notify renders nothing → backstop re-attaches `auto_update: true` from disk.

So the case that regresses: user cycles OFF→NOTIFY within a session (drops the key from file), then a later persistConfig in the same session re-renders `auto_update: false` from the stale booted `saved.autoUpdate == off`. The in-memory `saved` was never updated. The file flip-flops back to `off`. This is a genuine (if narrow) correctness gap: `persistConfig` should overlay the live `config.autoUpdate` (like it does for mode/approvalMode etc.), or the settings flow should update `saved`'s copy. Actually wait — does the settings flow update `saved`? `config.autoUpdate = next` — `config` here is the AgentCliConfig (live), not `saved` (the CliConfig captured in the closure). So yes, `saved` stays stale.

Hmm, but is this within scope of this PR? The PR claims: "compaction: rides along from the LOADED global value only — never the settings-hub live override or a project pick — so the documented no-leak guarantee holds". For compaction that's INTENTIONAL (session scope promises no file change). For auto_update, the settings flow EXPLICITLY writes the global file — it's a global-scope pick — so carrying the boot-loaded value and NOT the live value means the next save reverts the user's file-level change. Before this PR: same revert happened (key dropped entirely, both `on` and `off` choices lost). So this PR doesn't make that specific case worse — for `off→notify` it actually makes it WORSE in a subtle way: before, the key vanished (matching the user's intent — notify is default), after, the key comes back as `auto_update: false` (contradicting the user's intent). Let me double check: user boots with `auto_update: off` in file. `saved.autoUpdate == off`. User cycles: notify→... wait the flow cycles based on `config.autoUpdate` which at boot == off (loaded). Cycle: off → notify → `_dropAutoUpdateKey()` removes the line from the file. `config.autoUpdate = notify`. Now a later persistConfig: `saved.copyWith(...)` — `saved.autoUpdate` is still `off` → `_autoUpdateYaml()` renders `auto_update: false` → merged output differs from disk → file rewritten with `auto_update: false`. User wanted `notify` (no key). Regression of the user's mid-session change.

Before PR: boot `auto_update: off`; cycle off→notify → key dropped from file; later persistConfig: fresh CliConfig, autoUpdate default notify → renders nothing → old backstop: `auto_update` NOT in the set → nothing re-attached → file keeps no key → user intent PRESERVED (by accident). So yes — this PR introduces a regression for this specific flow (off→notify within a session, then any other persist trigger). Narrow but real. Severity: IMPORTANT (not blocking — narrow window, self-heals on next boot; the file keeps `auto_update: false` which is a wrong-but-valid setting; the user sees auto-update still off when they chose notify). Hmm — actually wait, is it worse than IMPORTANT? The user's choice is silently reverted — a real correctness bug of the same class the PR claims to fix ("a save can never reset a field the boot did not mention"). The irony: the PR fixes dropped sections but the same closure-capture pattern can now RESURRECT a setting the user cleared mid-session. I'd rate it IMPORTANT — it requires the settings-hub flow plus a subsequent persist in the same session.

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are

+        misuseBreaker &&

...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.
