So `agent.mode` (yaml) → `agentLoadMode` AND when `pi` → also `agentMode`. The renderer writes `mode: $agentLoadMode` but NOT `agentMode`. If agentMode == 'pi' then agentLoadMode == 'pi' too (per the doc: "when it is pi, also on CliConfig.agentMode"). So rendering mode: $agentLoadMode covers agentMode == pi. What if agentMode is set but agentLoadMode is null? Per the doc, agentMode only gets set when mode==pi, which also sets agentLoadMode. The settings-hub harness-mode pick writes the yaml directly (upsert) — the live `config.agentMode` is updated? Looking at harness mode flow: `_applyHarnessModePick` does `_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'], picked, ...)` — it does NOT update config.agentMode in memory ("the running session keeps its boot mode"). OK.

So the emitter renders `mode: $agentLoadMode` — covers agentMode=pi. Fine.

Now the key issue confirmed: after this PR, `agent:` IS re-rendered from `saved` by the boot save, so the `_clearContextCap` flow's file-level removal gets reverted by the next persist in the same session. Also `_dropAutoUpdateKey` for auto_update.

Wait, actually — let me re-check `_clearContextCap`: does it also update the live `config`? The write branch for SETTING the cap does `if (wrote) _warnCapNoOp(value)`. The CLEAR branch — from the code above — just writes the file. Doesn't touch config. And `persistConfig` uses `saved`, not `config`, for contextWindowCap. So yes: boot with cap → clear cap in settings → later `/mode` switch (persistConfig) → cap re-written to file. Also even simpler: `_clearContextCap` writes the file; then the user switches mode → persist → file rewritten with `agent: contextWindowCap` from `saved`. Confirmed.

Hmm, one more check — does `persistConfig` even get called after `_clearContextCap` in the same session? persistConfig triggers: onModeChanged, onApprovalChanged, onToolsConfigChanged, onSkillTogglesChanged, onModelsConfigChanged, onCubeSettingsChanged, skillsAccess dialog, startup dialog... yes, plenty. Even the boot call itself happens BEFORE any of these flows (line 1614 runs at boot).

Also note: the boot `persistConfig()` call at line 1614 — for a file where `agent.contextWindowCap` exists, `saved` carries it, emitter renders it, output == disk (if canonical) → no write. Good — that's the PR's headline fix.

Now let me ALSO check the `tui:` section for a reset flow: settings flow with theme? Let me search for tui theme reset. And quota/power/trajectory/subagents/jobs/headless/waiting flows — any removal flows for those? `_dropTopLevelBlock` usages: only 'agent' and 'auto_update'. So only those two flows are affected by the stale-snapshot resurrection.

But ALSO — what about sections like `spills:` where the emitter now renders from saved? If the user hand-edits the file mid-session (removes `spills:`), the next persist re-renders from `saved` (boot snapshot) — resurrection of boot state over mid-session hand edits. But that was TRUE BEFORE the PR for carried sections (memory, redact, a2a... were passed explicitly as saved.X). So mid-session hand edits were already doomed for those; the PR extends the same semantics to more sections. This is the fundamental "stale snapshot whole-file rewrite" tension, mitigated only for customProviders. The PR does not make that philosophy worse per se — it makes the emitted content match boot state more completely. The removal flows are the sharp edge: they're the ONLY sanctioned mid-session file mutations besides customProviders/toggles, and two of them (agent-cap clear, auto_update drop) now get clobbered.

But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. `AgentCliConfig` has mutable `autoUpdate` (the settings flow sets `config.autoUpdate = next`) and `contextWindowCap` (final). So the fix directions:
- `autoUpdate`: persistConfig could overlay `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` — the live field is maintained by the flow. But careful: is AgentCliConfig.autoUpdate ONLY mutated by the global flow? settings_flow_auto_update cycles the GLOBAL policy (writes global file, no scope pick). Yes — the auto-update flow is global-only. So overlaying `cli.config.autoUpdate` is safe and fixes the auto_update revert.
- `contextWindowCap`: AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap is final, and `_clearContextCap` doesn't update it. Would need the flow to update `saved` or expose a mutable field.
- `compaction`: session-scope live override must not persist; global/project writes go through the file. The cleanest fix is re-syncing `saved` after sanctioned file writes (e.g. a hook the flows call, or making `saved` a mutable var reloaded after `_upsertConfigYaml` global writes / `_drop*` writes).

I'll present the root cause + fix directions in the comment; the author picks.

Now the remaining review dimensions. Let me look at the full new `copyWith` doc and check one more edge in `saveCliConfig`: `_configTmpCounter` incremented even when skipping — no wait, short-circuit returns BEFORE constructing tmp — good.

Another check — `saveCliConfig` skip means the `.fah` dir may be created but file never created when diskText '' and finalText ''? If config doesn't exist and the config to save renders non-empty (typical), file is created. If it renders EMPTY (all-default CliConfig)... can't happen — toYaml always renders provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode. Fine.

Now, the unchanged-save skip: is `finalText == diskText` the right notion of "unchanged"? finalText is derived as `_preserveDiskSections(diskText, merged.toYaml())`. If disk has sections in a different ORDER than the emitter would render but identical content — the emitted text is compared against the FULL disk text, so any ordering difference → rewrite (canonicalization) once, then stable. Matches the PR note. OK.

What about file permissions? rename replaces the file — pre-existing behavior.

Windows: rename-over failed → delete+rename — unchanged.

Now the `test` dimension: 6 new tests, meaningful assertions, all failed pre-fix per the PR description. The unchanged-save test uses mtime — with 50ms delay; reasonable on CI? mtime granularity on some filesystems is 1s — a rewrite within the same second would NOT bump mtime → false pass? No wait — the test expects mtime UNCHANGED. If a rewrite happened but fs mtime granularity is coarse (1s), lastModifiedSync might return the same value → the assertion would PASS even though the file was rewritten — but they also assert text equality which would still pass (content identical). The mtime pin could be a vacuous pass on coarse-mtime filesystems. They added a 50ms delay to "give the filesystem clock room" — on ext4 with ns timestamps fine; on HFS+/coarse fs the test could vacuously pass. Minor test-robustness nit — SUGGESTION. blocks.text:
**Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are
+  /// never written so the file stays minimal.
   String _agentSectionYaml() {
     final stuckYaml = _stuckToolYaml();
     if (contextWindowCap == null &&
         agentLoadMode == null &&
+        misuseBreaker &&
         stuckYaml.isEmpty) {
       return '';
     }
...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.

Post-PR: the breaker flag survives (good — that's a fix), BUT:
(a) `validateAgentSection` (fa config check / config set / settings-hub upsert validation) now FAILS on the newly-rendered file: `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The validator mirrors the boot parser "pinned by test" — and the PR added the render+parse but did NOT update the mirror validator. Let me verify there's a pin test: "Mirrors the strict private parser in cli_config.dart (pinned by test)" — and the PR didn't touch config_service.dart (not in the changed-file list). So yes — post-PR, any config with `misuseBreaker: false`:
   - `fa config check` reports failed (a false positive on a file fa itself wrote).
   - settings-hub agent-section upserts (harness mode pick, context cap set) validate the whole agent section → refuse to save ("not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker").
   - the agent `config` tool set with any agent key → same refusal.

A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

messages.preview: Found a validator mirror gap. Let me verify how `_upsertConfigYaml` validates the agent section.

blocks.text:
**Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are
+  /// never written so the file stays minimal.
   String _agentSectionYaml() {
     final stuckYaml = _stuckToolYaml();
     if (contextWindowCap == null &&
         agentLoadMode == null &&
+        misuseBreaker &&
         stuckYaml.isEmpty) {
       return '';
     }
...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.

Post-PR: the breaker flag survives (good — that's a fix), BUT:
(a) `validateAgentSection` (fa config check / config set / settings-hub upsert validation) now FAILS on the newly-rendered file: `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The validator mirrors the boot parser "pinned by test" — and the PR added the render+parse but did NOT update the mirror validator. Let me verify there's a pin test: "Mirrors the strict private parser in cli_config.dart (pinned by test)" — and the PR didn't touch config_service.dart (not in the changed-file list). So yes — post-PR, any config with `misuseBreaker: false`:
   - `fa config check` reports failed (a false positive on a file fa itself wrote).
   - settings-hub agent-section upserts (harness mode pick, context cap set) validate the whole agent section → refuse to save ("not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker").
   - the agent `config` tool set with any agent key → same refusal.

Let me verify _upsertConfigYaml validates the whole section. Let me read it.

blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

But careful: is AgentCliConfig.autoUpdate ONLY mutated by the global flow? settings_flow_auto_update cycles the GLOBAL policy (writes global file, no scope pick). Yes — the auto-update flow is global-only. So overlaying `cli.config.autoUpdate` is safe and fixes the auto_update revert.
- `contextWindowCap`: AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap is final, and `_clearContextCap` doesn't update it. Would need the flow to update `saved` or expose a mutable field.
- `compaction`: session-scope live override must not persist; global/project writes go through the file. The cleanest fix is re-syncing `saved` after sanctioned file writes (e.g. a hook the flows call, or making `saved` a mutable var reloaded after `_upsertConfigYaml` global writes / `_drop*` writes).

I'll present the root cause + fix directions in the comment; the author picks.

If disk has sections in a different ORDER than the emitter would render but identical content — the emitted text is compared against the FULL disk text, so any ordering difference → rewrite (canonicalization) once, then stable. Windows: rename-over failed → delete+rename — unchanged.

The unchanged-save test uses mtime — with 50ms delay; reasonable on CI? mtime granularity on some filesystems is 1s — a rewrite within the same second would NOT bump mtime → false pass? No wait — the test expects mtime UNCHANGED. If a rewrite happened but fs mtime granularity is coarse (1s), lastModifiedSync might return the same value → the assertion would PASS even though the file was rewritten — but they also assert text equality which would still pass (content identical). They added a 50ms delay to "give the filesystem clock room" — on ext4 with ns timestamps fine; on HFS+/coarse fs the test could vacuously pass. Minor test-robustness nit — SUGGESTION. **Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are
+  /// never written so the file stays minimal.

     final stuckYaml = _stuckToolYaml();

+        misuseBreaker &&

       return '';

...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.

Post-PR: the breaker flag survives (good — that's a fix), BUT:
(a) `validateAgentSection` (fa config check / config set / settings-hub upsert validation) now FAILS on the newly-rendered file: `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The validator mirrors the boot parser "pinned by test" — and the PR added the render+parse but did NOT update the mirror validator. Let me verify there's a pin test: "Mirrors the strict private parser in cli_config.dart (pinned by test)" — and the PR didn't touch config_service.dart (not in the changed-file list).    - the agent `config` tool set with any agent key → same refusal.

Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

**Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are
+  /// never written so the file stays minimal.
   String _agentSectionYaml() {
     final stuckYaml = _stuckToolYaml();
     if (contextWindowCap == null &&
         agentLoadMode == null &&
+        misuseBreaker &&
         stuckYaml.isEmpty) {
       return '';
     }
...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.

Post-PR: the breaker flag survives (good — that's a fix), BUT:
(a) `validateAgentSection` (fa config check / config set / settings-hub upsert validation) now FAILS on the newly-rendered file: `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The validator mirrors the boot parser "pinned by test" — and the PR added the render+parse but did NOT update the mirror validator. Let me verify there's a pin test: "Mirrors the strict private parser in cli_config.dart (pinned by test)" — and the PR didn't touch config_service.dart (not in the changed-file list). A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Same for `agent:` block with hand comments: post-PR emitter renders typed subset → comments lost once. Documented. OK — SUGGESTION-level at most, arguably by design.

Now `waiting:` — no renderer, backstop only. Boot save: saved.waiting parsed but never rendered → omitted → backstop re-attaches raw block. Fine.

What about sections in `_diskPreservedSections` that are rendered only conditionally — `subagents` renders when heartbeat/stall non-default; if user's on-disk subagents block has NON-default values, saved carries them → rendered → fine.

`quota`: `QuotaSection` default; test uses `badge: true, ttl_minutes: 30`. Renderer `_quotaYaml` — presumably renders non-defaults. Fine.

A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

blocks.text:
**Confirmed.** Both regressions reproduce:

1. `_clearContextCap` (settings → clear context cap, drops `agent:` block from file) → any later `persistConfig()` in the same session (mode switch, approval change, skills toggle…) re-renders `agent: contextWindowCap: 256000` from the stale boot snapshot — the user's removal is silently reverted.
2. `_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings → auto update cycle off→notify, drops `auto_update:` from file) → later persist re-adds `auto_update: false`.

Before this PR these removals stuck (the fresh-CliConfig emitter rendered neither key and the old backstop didn't re-attach them). So the PR trades "boot drops sections" for "same-session removals resurrect". The removal flows' contract ("contextWindowCap removed → file", "auto_update removed → notify is the default") is broken by the next save.

Severity: this is a correctness bug introduced by the diff — the settings flows' documented behavior ("removed → …", "everything else survives byte-for-byte") is broken. Per the verdict rules this is 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug). It's the same class of bug as the ticket itself (config file not honoring user intent). It affects two settings-hub flows.

Wait — one consideration: were these removal flows EVER safe before gh-1572? Let me re-verify the pre-PR behavior with a quick check on the base commit. Actually I reasoned through the code: pre-PR persistConfig fresh CliConfig without contextWindowCap/autoUpdate → emitter omits both → old backstop (memory, cube, roles, ttsr, prompts, redact, compaction, a2a, providerTimeouts, images, fabric, mcp, links, output) doesn't include agent/auto_update → removals stuck. I could verify by `git stash`-free worktree... Actually I can verify by checking out base cli_config.dart + fah_runapp.dart into a temp dir? Simpler: `git worktree`? AGENTS.md says avoid. I can simulate the old persist shape in my scratch test: `saveCliConfig(tmp, CliConfig(mode:'code', approvalMode:'yolo', allowedTools:[]))` after the drop — with the NEW code the backstop includes agent/auto_update but the emitter (fresh CliConfig) doesn't render them → re-attached → also resurrects! Wait — that's the "disk backstop" test behavior — deliberate. Hmm! So even the OLD persist shape now resurrects (because the backstop now includes agent/auto_update).

blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

But wait — is agentMode ALWAYS equal to agentLoadMode when set? `_parseAgentSection`: `mode = _parseAgentModeValue(node[key])` → returns agentLoadMode=mode; agentMode = (mode == 'pi') ? 'pi' : null presumably. So agentMode ⊆ agentLoadMode. Render covers it. Good.

If user explicitly wrote `classic: false` in the file, emitter omits → backstop re-attaches raw block only if the emitter rendered NO tui section... if tuiTheme set but classic:false explicit → emitter renders `tui:\n  theme: ...\n` (no classic) → the explicit `classic: false` is dropped — semantics preserved (false == default). The unchanged-save skip reduces write churn — no security impact. The spill toYaml renders only scalars. No injection risk (yaml scalar rendering of ints/bools only). Good.

8. Backward compat: first-boot canonicalization documented. `withCustomProviders` behavior preserved (signature same). `copyWith` new public method — additive. `SpillsConfig.toYaml` new public — additive. OK.

So the PR trades "boot drops sections" for "same-session removals resurrect". The removal flows' contract ("contextWindowCap removed → file", "auto_update removed → notify is the default") is broken by the next save.

blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Same for `agent:` block with hand comments: post-PR emitter renders typed subset → comments lost once. Documented. OK — SUGGESTION-level at most, arguably by design.

Now `waiting:` — no renderer, backstop only. Boot save: saved.waiting parsed but never rendered → omitted → backstop re-attaches raw block. Fine.

What about sections in `_diskPreservedSections` that are rendered only conditionally — `subagents` renders when heartbeat/stall non-default; if user's on-disk subagents block has NON-default values, saved carries them → rendered → fine.

`quota`: `QuotaSection` default; test uses `badge: true, ttl_minutes: 30`. Renderer `_quotaYaml` — presumably renders non-defaults. Fine.

Now let me also check `power:` — `power.hold` has `PowerAssertionHold` with value 'session'. `_powerYaml` renders `hold:`? saw partial: sleepPrevention + presumably hold. Fine.

Next dimension: the `fetchLatestTag` reformat — pure formatter noise, unrelated to the fix. SUG…

blocks.text:
**Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). 🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

`_agentSectionYaml()` newly renders `misuseBreaker: false` (good — before this PR the kill switch was silently dropped by every save). But `validateAgentSection` in `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` — the mirror validator used by `fa config check`, `fa config set agent.*`, and the settings-hub agent upserts (`validate: validateAgentSection` in settings_flow.dart / settings_flow_harness_mode.dart) — only knows `contextWindowCap` and `mode`; any other key throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. 2. Settings → Harness mode / context-cap writes validate the whole `agent:` section through `_upsertConfigYaml` → **"not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker"** — the flow is broken for that user until they hand-edit the file.
