blocks.text:
Confirmed a THIRD instance, and this one is on the PR's own claimed-invariant ground:

**Compaction global-scope pick reverted.** The PR comment in persistConfig explicitly claims: "`compaction:` rides along from [saved] — the LOADED global value, never the settings-hub's live override or a project-scope pick, so a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file." But consider the GLOBAL scope pick: `_applyCompactionEngineScope('global')` writes `compaction:\n  engine: X` into `~/.fah/config.yaml` via `_upsertConfigYaml` (the sanctioned global write). `saved.compactionEngine` is the boot-loaded value. A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

Same pattern. So the general finding: **persistConfig's saved.copyWith base reverts sanctioned mid-session global-file writes (settings-hub flows) for every section it renders from the stale boot snapshot** — concretely reproducible for `agent.contextWindowCap` clear, `auto_update` drop, and global compaction picks that change a non-default boot value.

Hmm wait, for compaction let me be careful about _upsertConfigYaml and whether the compaction global flow ALSO triggers persistConfig immediately... The flow writes the file, sets live override. persistConfig is only called by hooks. So the revert happens on the NEXT hook fire.

Before PR, persistConfig rendered compaction how? The old code did NOT pass compactionEngine/compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds (fresh CliConfig defaults null) → _compactionYaml '' → backstop had 'compaction' → re-attach on-disk block. So pre-PR the global pick SURVIVED. Post-PR it's reverted (when boot value was rendered/non-default). Definite regression #3. This one directly contradicts the PR's own comment claim ("a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — true, but the inverse leak: the global file's new value gets re-leaked-over by the boot snapshot).

Severity: all three are the same root cause. I'll write ONE blocking inline comment describing the root cause with the three concrete manifestations (agent-cap clear + auto_update drop verified by repro; compaction global pick by code analysis).

Root cause restated: `persistConfig`'s base `saved` is a boot-time snapshot; several settings-hub flows legitimately mutate the global FILE mid-session without updating `saved` or the live `cli.config` fields that persistConfig overlays; the next persist re-renders the snapshot over those writes. Fix options: (a) overlay the live fields the settings flows DO maintain (`config.autoUpdate`, `config.contextWindowCap`, `config.liveCompactionEngine` for... no — liveCompactionEngine may be session-scoped! Persisting the live override would break the session-scope "no file change" promise... careful: for compaction, session-scope sets liveCompactionEngine but must NOT write the file; global/project-scope ALSO set liveCompactionEngine after the file write. So persisting liveCompactionEngine is wrong (would leak session picks). The correct fix for compaction: exclude `compaction` from the render when it equals the boot-loaded value... hmm, actually simplest: the settings flows should update a host-held "session saved config" — e.g. `_runApp` could expose `saved` mutator, or persistConfig could re-read the file... Overkill for a review — I'll suggest directions: overlay live-maintained fields (autoUpdate, contextWindowCap) and for compaction keep the old omit-and-backstop behavior (don't render compaction in persistConfig at all — the backstop preserves the block; note that with copyWith-base the field is non-null when loaded... so they'd need a way to emit nothing for compaction: e.g. rebuild saved-copy with compaction fields null? copyWith can't clear (null=keep)! That's exactly the copyWith-can't-clear limitation biting. They could add a `compaction: CompactionSection?` object param or a dedicated `withoutCompactionRender` flag... or persistConfig could construct the base differently: `saved.copyWith(...)` then the emitter could take a "render these sections raw-from-disk" list. Cleanest minimal fix: have the settings flows route their global writes through a callback that ALSO updates the in-memory `saved` (a `onGlobalConfigEdited` hook re-running `saved = loadCliConfig(home)`); since `saved` is `late final`, it'd need to become mutable — trivial in _runApp.)

OK. That's my BLOCKING finding #1.

Now — the mtime-based "no write at boot" check `finalText == diskText`: any subtlety about the first-boot canonicalization? PR notes admit the first boot may canonicalize once. Fine.

Next: check `_preserveDiskSections` interplay with the short-circuit: if the emitter rendered a section and the disk had a DIFFERENT raw block (e.g. comments inside the block), the emitted wins and the user's comments inside that block are lost — pre-existing semantics ("caller wins wherever it rendered"), now applying to more sections (agent, tui, quota, spills...). E.g. a user's hand-written `tui:` block with comments + future keys: boot loads typed values, emitter re-renders typed subset → comments/future keys in the tui block LOST on first boot. Pre-PR: tui wasn't rendered nor backstopped... wait pre-PR tui WAS rendered by the emitter (tui section renderer existed — `_tuiSectionYaml` at line ~1045 pre-PR? The diff shows `_tuiSectionYaml` unchanged (not in diff), so yes pre-PR rendered tui from... the FRESH CliConfig which passed NOTHING for tui → defaults → omitted. So pre-PR: tui omitted → backstop lacked tui → user's whole tui block DROPPED on boot (the ticket bug). Post-PR: tui rendered from saved (typed subset) → comments within the tui block lost, but values preserved. Acceptable, matches the documented "first boot may canonicalize once" note.

Same for `agent:` block with hand comments: post-PR emitter renders typed subset → comments lost once. Documented. OK — SUGGESTION-level at most, arguably by design.

Now `waiting:` — no renderer, backstop only. Boot save: saved.waiting parsed but never rendered → omitted → backstop re-attaches raw block. Fine.

What about sections in `_diskPreservedSections` that are rendered only conditionally — `subagents` renders when heartbeat/stall non-default; if user's on-disk subagents block has NON-default values, saved carries them → rendered → fine.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. 3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the mtime pin can pass vacuously on coarse-clock filesystems**

`an unchanged save does not rewrite the file` asserts `lastModifiedSync() == before` after a 50 ms delay. On filesystems with coarse (1 s) mtime granularity a real rewrite inside the same clock tick would not bump the mtime and the assertion would pass vacuously (the content compare cannot distinguish a rewrite from a skip — the rewritten bytes are identical by definition). A stronger signal that stays portable: assert the short-circuit directly — e.g. wrap the second save with a `File('${path}.tmp.')` glob check (no temp residue), or expose/spy the write chain, or `FileStat`-compare `ino`/`mode` before/after. Low priority — on the CI runners (ext4, ns timestamps) the current form is effective.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

A later `persistConfig()` in the same session renders `compaction:` from the stale `saved` → emitter renders the section (when saved has non-default engine/judge) → "caller wins" → the user's global pick is overwritten with the boot value. Pre-PR, persistConfig omitted compaction and the backstop (`compaction` was already in `_diskPreservedSections`) re-attached the on-disk block → the pick survived.

Concrete: boot config has `compaction:\n  engine: classic`. `saved.compactionEngine == classic`. User settings → Compaction → global → structured. Upsert writes `compaction:\n  engine: structured` to the file. Then `/mode` switch (or skills toggle...) → persistConfig → emitter renders `compaction:\n  engine: classic` (from saved) → file rewritten → user's structured pick reverted to classic.

Or: boot with NO compaction section (saved default null) → user picks global classic → file gets `compaction: engine: classic` → next persist: saved.compactionEngine == null → emitter omits compaction → backstop re-attaches on-disk block → SURVIVES. So the revert only bites when the boot-loaded engine/judge was NON-default (rendered) and differs from the new pick — e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudgetSeconds change with a different engine... judgeBudget: settings flow for judge budget writes `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` upsert; saved.compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds is boot value; if boot had `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` and user changes to 900 via upsert, next persist re-renders `judgeBudgetSeconds: 600` (rendered since non-default) → reverted.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot-time `saved` snapshot now re-renders over sanctioned mid-session config edits — settings-hub removals/global picks are silently reverted**

`persistConfig` now uses the boot-loaded `saved` as the copyWith base, and the emitter renders `agent:`, `auto_update:` and `compaction:` from it. But several settings-hub flows legitimately write `~/.fah/config.yaml` **directly, mid-session**, without updating `saved` (it is a `late final` loaded once at boot) or the fields this overlay carries. The next `persistConfig()` trigger in the same session (`/mode` switch, approval change, skill toggle, models/cube change…) re-renders the stale boot values over those edits. I verified both of these with a runnable repro against this branch:

1. **`_clearContextCap` (settings_flow.dart:2062) is undone.** Boot with `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` → settings → clear cap (drops the whole `agent:` block from the file, verified on disk) → any later persist → the file contains `agent:\n  contextWindowCap: 256000` again. Repro: reload after the next `saveCliConfig` returns `contextWindowCap == 256000`, expected `null`. Before this PR the removal stuck (the fresh-`CliConfig` emitter rendered no `agent:` section and `agent` was not in `_diskPreservedSections`).

2. **`_dropAutoUpdateKey` (settings_flow_auto_update.dart:44) is undone.** Boot with `auto_update: false` → settings → Auto update cycle off→notify (the key line is dropped, "notify is the default") → any later persist → the file contains `auto_update: false` again. Repro: reload returns `AutoUpdateMode.off`, expected `notify`.

3. **Global compaction picks are reverted the same way** (code-verified): settings → Compaction → scope **global** writes `compaction:\n  engine: …` via the sanctioned `_upsertConfigYaml`, but a later persist renders `compaction:` from `saved.compactionEngine` (the boot value) — and since the emitter rendered it, the backstop does not re-attach the newer block. Whenever the boot-loaded engine/judgeBudgetSeconds was non-default and differs from the pick (e.g. classic → structured, or a judgeBudget change), the user's global pick is overwritten. Pre-PR the emitter omitted `compaction:` and the backstop preserved the upsert-written block, so the pick survived. Note the new comment's claim — "a session/project selection cannot leak into the global file" — holds, but the inverse now happens: the global file's newer value is overwritten by the boot snapshot.

The `saved.copyWith` base is the right shape for the ticket's headline bug; the gap is that the boot snapshot can go stale against the three flows that mutate the global file outside `persistConfig`. Suggested directions (your pick):

- Overlay the live-maintained fields the same way `mode`/`approvalMode` are: `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` fixes case 2 (the field is already mutated by the flow). Cases 1 and 3 need the snapshot refreshed, since `AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap` is final and `liveCompactionEngine` must stay unpersisted (session scope promises no file change).
- Cleaner general fix: make `saved` mutable and re-sync it (`saved = loadCliConfig(home)`) after every sanctioned direct file write (`_clearContextCap`, `_dropAutoUpdateKey`, global/project `_upsertConfigYaml` wins, `_removeCapabilityYaml`) — via the existing hook pattern. Then every save renders the freshest on-disk truth and this whole class closes.

Please also add a regression test pinning "settings-hub removal/global write survives the next persist in the same session" (see the test-coverage comment).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa` now writes `agent.misuseBreaker: false`, but the strict mirror validator rejects it — `fa config check` false-fails and settings-hub agent upserts refuse to save**

`_agentSectionYaml()` newly renders `misuseBreaker: false` (good — before this PR the kill switch was silently dropped by every save). But `validateAgentSection` in `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` — the mirror validator used by `fa config check`, `fa config set agent.*`, and the settings-hub agent upserts (`validate: validateAgentSection` in settings_flow.dart / settings_flow_harness_mode.dart) — only knows `contextWindowCap` and `mode`; any other key throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The PR does not touch `config_service.dart`.

Verified against this branch with a repro: `validateAgentSection` on the exact block this PR's emitter writes (`agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n`) throws. Consequences for a user who disabled the misuse breaker:

1. First boot after this fix re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` → every subsequent `fa config check` reports **failed** on a file `fa` itself wrote (false positive; also poisons the `config` tool's `check` op for agents).
2. Settings → Harness mode / context-cap writes validate the whole `agent:` section through `_upsertConfigYaml` → **"not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker"** — the flow is broken for that user until they hand-edit the file.
3. Same for the `config` tool's `set agent.…`.

Fix: add a `misuseBreaker` case to `validateAgentSection` mirroring `_parseAgentMisuseBreakerValue` (boolean, in `cli_config.dart`), and extend the "pins against cli_config.dart" test group so the mirror cannot drift again. The emitter must never produce a document the boot parser accepts but `config check` rejects.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the two regression classes this PR opens have no pinning tests**

The 6 new tests are solid on the ticket's own scenarios (round-trip, boot-shaped overlay, spills render, backstop, no-op save). But this branch also fails two scenarios no test exercises — both verified broken by repro during review:

1. **A sanctioned mid-session file edit survives the next persist.** Boot-shaped `saveCliConfig` immediately after `_clearContextCap`-style file edit (`agent:` block dropped) re-adds the cap; same for `_dropAutoUpdateKey` (`auto_update` dropped → re-added as `false`) and for a global compaction pick that differs from a non-default boot value. The ticket's expectation "Saving never drops a known section" needs its inverse pinned too: *"a removal/global write performed by the settings flows is never resurrected by a later save in the same session."*
2. **Everything the emitter renders passes `validateAgentSection`.** The emitter now writes `agent.misuseBreaker: false`, which the mirror validator rejects — `fa config check` false-fails on fa's own output. There is an existing "pins against cli_config.dart" pattern in the config_service tests; add the `misuseBreaker` case there so emitter↔validator parity is enforced mechanically (this is exactly the drift class the `copyWith` refactor just eliminated for the constructor — same medicine for the validator).

Both tests fail on the current head, which is the point: they convert the two review blockers into red-first regressions.

- `autoUpdate`: persistConfig could overlay `autoUpdate: cli.config.autoUpdate` — the live field is maintained by the flow. But careful: is AgentCliConfig.autoUpdate ONLY mutated by the global flow? settings_flow_auto_update cycles the GLOBAL policy (writes global file, no scope pick). Yes — the auto-update flow is global-only. So overlaying `cli.config.autoUpdate` is safe and fixes the auto_update revert.
- `contextWindowCap`: AgentCliConfig.contextWindowCap is final, and `_clearContextCap` doesn't update it. Would need the flow to update `saved` or expose a mutable field.
- `compaction`: session-scope live override must not persist; global/project writes go through the file. The cleanest fix is re-syncing `saved` after sanctioned file writes (e.g. a hook the flows call, or making `saved` a mutable var reloaded after `_upsertConfigYaml` global writes / `_drop*` writes).

I'll present the root cause + fix directions in the comment; the author picks.

Now the remaining review dimensions. Let me look at the full new `copyWith` doc and check one more edge in `saveCliConfig`: `_configTmpCounter` incremented even when skipping — no wait, short-circuit returns BEFORE constructing tmp — good.

Another check — `saveCliConfig` skip means the `.fah` dir may be created but file never created when diskText '' and finalText ''? If config doesn't exist and the config to save renders non-empty (typical), file is created. If it renders EMPTY (all-default CliConfig)... can't happen — toYaml always renders provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode. Fine.

Now, the unchanged-save skip: is `finalText == diskText` the right notion of "unchanged"? finalText is derived as `_preserveDiskSections(diskText, merged.toYaml())`. If disk has sections in a different ORDER than the emitter would render but identical content — the emitted text is compared against the FULL disk text, so any ordering difference → rewrite (canonicalization) once, then stable. Matches the PR note. OK.

What about file permissions? rename replaces the file — pre-existing behavior.

Windows: rename-over failed → delete+rename — unchanged.

Now the `test` dimension: 6 new tests, meaningful assertions, all failed pre-fix per the PR description. The unchanged-save test uses mtime — with 50ms delay; reasonable on CI? mtime granularity on some filesystems is 1s — a rewrite within the same second would NOT bump mtime → false pass? No wait — the test expects mtime UNCHANGED. If a rewrite happened but fs mtime granularity is coarse (1s), lastModifiedSync might return the same value → the assertion would PASS even though the file was rewritten — but they also assert text equality which would still pass (content identical). The mtime pin could be a vacuous pass on coarse-mtime filesystems. They added a 50ms delay to "give the filesystem clock room" — on ext4 with ns timestamps fine; on HFS+/coarse fs the test could vacuously pass. Minor test-robustness nit — SUGGESTION. Could assert no tmp file residue — weak. It's acceptable; keep as SUGGESTION.

Good — this is why null=keep works here.

BUT: `promptOverrides` etc. — `promptOverrides ?? this.promptOverrides` — same. persistConfig no longer passes promptOverrides — keeps saved's. Good.

One subtle thing in copyWith semantics: `mode: cli.currentMode.name` etc. — always non-null → fine.

blocks.text:
**Found a real gap**: `validateAgentSection` in config_service.dart (used by `fa config check` and the config tool's `set` validation, and the settings-hub `_upsertConfigYaml` validate path) does NOT know the `misuseBreaker` key — it throws `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`.

Consequences of the PR change:
1. `_agentSectionYaml()` now RENDERS `agent:\n  misuseBreaker: false\n` for a user who disabled the misuse breaker. But wait — how did a user disable the misuse breaker in the first place? Only by hand-editing the file (the boot parser accepts it). After the PR, the first boot SAVE re-renders the file with `misuseBreaker: false` (typed render). Now `fa config check` on that file → `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker` → **check FAILED**. Also the settings-hub agent flows (`_upsertConfigYaml(['agent','mode'|'contextWindowCap'], ..., validate: validateAgentSection)`) validate the WHOLE section? Let me check `_upsertConfigYaml` — it validates the edited doc's `agent` section with the validator → an `agent:` block containing `misuseBreaker: false` makes EVERY agent-section upsert REJECT: "not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker" — so after the first boot re-render, the settings-hub harness-mode/cap flows are BROKEN for users with the kill switch.

Wait — did the emitter render `misuseBreaker: false` BEFORE this PR? Let me check the base version of `_agentSectionYaml`:

From the diff:
```
-  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, or a stuck-tool
-  /// config is persisted; defaults are never written so the file stays
-  /// minimal.
+  /// The `agent:` section, only when a cap, a load mode, a stuck-tool
+  /// config, or the misuse-breaker kill switch is persisted; defaults are
+  /// never written so the file stays minimal.
   String _agentSectionYaml() {
     final stuckYaml = _stuckToolYaml();
     if (contextWindowCap == null &&
         agentLoadMode == null &&
+        misuseBreaker &&
         stuckYaml.isEmpty) {
       return '';
     }
...
+    if (!misuseBreaker) {
+      section.write('  misuseBreaker: false\n');
+    }
```

So pre-PR the emitter NEVER rendered misuseBreaker — but the parser ACCEPTED it from the file (base parser has `misuseBreaker` case — was that pre-existing? The diff of cli_config.dart only shows copyWith/withCustomProviders/toYaml/_agentSectionYaml/_spillsYaml/saveCliConfig/_diskPreservedSections changes. The `misuseBreaker` parse case at line 309-310 is NOT in the diff → pre-existing. So pre-PR: a hand-written `agent: {misuseBreaker: false}` block — how did it survive the pre-PR boot save? Pre-PR fresh CliConfig didn't carry misuseBreaker (default true) → emitter omitted agent section if no cap/loadMode/stuckTool... → backstop lacked 'agent' → the whole block was DROPPED on boot (part of the ticket bug: "agent" section listed in the ticket's dropped sections). If the block had cap+misuseBreaker: emitter rendered cap but NOT misuseBreaker → the kill switch was silently LOST (reset to true!) on the first save. So pre-PR the breaker flag could not survive a save at all.

Post-PR: the breaker flag survives (good — that's a fix), BUT:
(a) `validateAgentSection` (fa config check / config set / settings-hub upsert validation) now FAILS on the newly-rendered file: `unknown "agent" key: misuseBreaker`. The validator mirrors the boot parser "pinned by test" — and the PR added the render+parse but did NOT update the mirror validator. Let me verify there's a pin test: "Mirrors the strict private parser in cli_config.dart (pinned by test)" — and the PR didn't touch config_service.dart (not in the changed-file list). So yes — post-PR, any config with `misuseBreaker: false`:
   - `fa config check` reports failed (a false positive on a file fa itself wrote).
   - settings-hub agent-section upserts (harness mode pick, context cap set) validate the whole agent section → refuse to save ("not saved: unknown agent key: misuseBreaker").
   - the agent `config` tool set with any agent key → same refusal.

NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SAFETY SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN SAFETY --> EXAMPLES SAFETY --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges.

data.text:
You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a13655-2d34-7c00-8be9-6e03fc7acd3e/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Optionally provide a timeout in seconds. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total); retries appear as [bash attempt N]. Environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — the command keeps running as a job, you get its id immediately and are notified when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command that is still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed) so the user gets an answer right away.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image

tools.name: generate_video

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.
